spec_references.heading: Module-level declarations

spec_references.heading: Expressions
spec_references.detail: Start actions are listed, but standalone let expressions and service object constructor expressions are not listed.

spec_references.detail: Named worker declarations are not listed among supported statements.

reason: Mixed case: annotation declarations/attachments (including source, marker, repeated annotations), classes, services, listeners, enums, casts, ordinary expressions and start actions have spec support. The entire fixture also requires named worker declarations, a standalone let expression, a service object constructor expression, and a remote method in a service class, which are outside the enumerated support or its stated class-method scope. Whole-case classification is therefore feature, despite its primarily supported annotation-negative checks.
unsupported_constructs: Named worker declaration worker w1 in funcWithWorker (not covered by Statements).
Standalone let expression initializing b (query let clauses are supported, but standalone let expressions are not listed).
Service object constructor expression initializing serVar (not listed under Expressions).
remote function getName in service class ServiceClass2 (remote method definitions are stated supported for client classes).
test_design_notes: Large combined negative fixture mixes annotation validation with unsupported host constructs; isolate supported attachment locations before treating all failures as annotation bugs.

The annotations on increment: 1 + 2 and increment: y + 1 are marked @error even though y is a const and the spec supports annotation values evaluated from constant expressions and additive operators; these appear to be stale or overbroad expected-error markers.
Repeated @tainted and @v1 attachments mark only selected occurrences; exact diagnostic placement/multiplicity cannot be established from this source and subset spec alone.
Structured binding declarations in the final section should not be equated with the separately restricted destructuring assignment statement: these are declarations, not assignments.
